title: NIT Trichy Launches Tata AI Centre With Rs 10 Crore TCS Backing
excerpt: The Tata Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning will fund Ph.D. fellowships and research across healthcare, education, agriculture, smart cities and digital infrastructure.
body:
• NIT Tiruchirappalli has opened the Tata Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, backed by a Rs 10 crore commitment from TCS Foundation under its CSR programme.
  • TCS CEO and Managing Director K. Krithivasan inaugurated the centre on campus on November 6, 2026, according to Elets, reporting an official institute communication also carried by The Hindu.
  • The centre will work across healthcare, education, agriculture, smart cities and transportation, and digital infrastructure services, with five Ph.D. scholars inducted so far.
  • NIT Trichy's official brochure offered 12 full-time Ph.D. positions at the centre with a stipend of Rs 40,000 a month for three years.

The National Institute of Technology Tiruchirappalli (NIT Trichy) has opened the Tata Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, a research hub backed by a Rs 10 crore commitment from TCS Foundation under its corporate social responsibility programme. K. Krithivasan, CEO and Managing Director of Tata Consultancy Services, inaugurated the centre on the campus on Friday, November 6, 2026, according to a report by Elets digitalLEARNING based on an official communication from the institute that was also reported by The Hindu.

According to that report, the funding will go towards advanced research infrastructure and Ph.D. fellowships. The centre sits within NIT Trichy's wider AI effort: its Centre of Excellence in Artificial Intelligence describes itself as the institute's flagship platform for AI research, innovation, technology translation, skill enhancement and industry collaboration.

Five research domains, starting with health and farms

Elets reported that the Tata Centre is built around five applied research domains: healthcare, education, agriculture, smart cities and transportation, and digital infrastructure services. The institute's own Ph.D. admissions brochure for the centre lists a closely matching set of thrust areas — healthcare, smart cities and transportation, precision agriculture, education and digital infrastructure services — plus any other emerging domains related to artificial intelligence.

That applied focus matters for who benefits. The research is framed around sector problems rather than laboratory work alone, and the first cohort reflects the structure: as a first step, five Ph.D. research scholars have been inducted, one for each domain, Elets reported. Winners of a 36-hour hackathon and the newly inducted Ph.D. scholars were felicitated at the launch, the report added.

What Ph.D. scholars at the centre receive

The clearest detail on support for researchers comes from NIT Trichy's official Ph.D. admissions brochure for the Tata Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning. It offered 12 full-time, stipend-supported Ph.D. positions, designed, in the brochure's words, to nurture innovation and high-quality research across interdisciplinary domains. Selected candidates receive a monthly stipend of Rs 40,000 for a duration of three years, along with additional financial support for attending conferences, undertaking academic travel, and accessing advanced high-end computational and research facilities.

The brochure describes the initiative as reflecting NIT Tiruchirappalli's continued commitment to fostering excellence in research and developing skilled professionals capable of addressing real-world challenges through artificial intelligence. Applications for the July 2026 session were invited through the institute's official admissions portal, with a last date of May 20, 2026, listed in the brochure — a timeline that places the scholar selection ahead of the centre's formal inauguration in November.

Partnerships signed at the launch

The inauguration was also used to widen the centre's research network. Elets reported that the institute signed Memoranda of Understanding with AgriX, described as a non-profit deep-tech think tank working on agriculture, and with the International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore, with a focus on digital public infrastructure. A tripartite collaboration between NIT Trichy, SASTRA Deemed University and Maharana Pratap Institute, Gorakhpur, was also highlighted at the event.

NIT Trichy Director G. Aghila and SASTRA Vice-Chancellor S. Vaidyasubramaniam attended the event along with senior officials of TCS and TCS Foundation, according to the report. Chandra Mohan Malladi, Global Head of Digital Public Infrastructure and Digital Platforms at TCS, also addressed the gathering.

Responsible AI in the inaugural address

In his inaugural address, as summarised by Elets, Krithivasan traced how quickly AI and machine learning have moved since generative AI platforms such as ChatGPT arrived. He said AI is no longer just a productivity tool and could enable solutions beyond what people can achieve today, and he stressed that ethical values must be built into how AI is developed and used, describing responsible adoption as a shared human responsibility.

For students and researchers, the immediate offer is concrete: funded doctoral positions, high-end computing, and work spanning classrooms, clinics, farms, cities and public digital platforms. With Rs 10 crore in CSR backing and its first five scholars in place, the Tata Centre at NIT Tiruchirappalli is now formally open.
